# VIX term structure — development report

**Family:** `vix-term-structure`  
**Directory:** `research/new/family-vix-term-structure/`  
**Window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 (development only). No 2024-2026 data
enters any signal, result or robustness calculation; the external series are
truncated at the development end before the features are computed.  
**Headline marks:** 1-minute panel, next-session 09:30 open, 2% band, 1 bp
headline cost; 5 bp and 10 bp reported.  
**Pre-registration:** `HYPOTHESIS.md`.

## Verdict (short)

**Qualified pass on the pre-registered development bar, with a weak placebo and
a severe 2022 drawdown.** At 1 bp the strategy earns **48.82% CAGR, 65.45% max
drawdown and 1.080 Sharpe** versus the TQQQ bar of **36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82**.
It has **165 fills**, 82 state changes, 41 round trips and 79.3% average TQQQ
exposure. Six of the eight pre-registered box cells clear the bar, the
circular-shift placebo is significant at 10% (p = 0.074 for the signal shift,
p = 0.054 for the matched state-path shift), and the maximum correlation with
the nine winners is 0.735.

The pass is not clean. The 2022 calendar year is **-55.9%**; the max drawdown is
a **63.3% peak-to-trough** fall from 2021-11-19 to 2022-06-16 on session-end
marks (65.45% intraday). The term-structure signal did not anticipate the slow
2022 bear market: it reacted to vol spikes, re-entered on calm, and was
whipsawed through the H1 2022 bear rallies. The edge is a handful of large
regime calls (2018, 2020, 2022 relative), not a consistent monthly timing rule.
It should go to a one-shot holdout only as a diversifying regime overlay, not as
a crash shield.

## 1. What was tested

The VIX/VIX3M ratio is the shape of the implied-vol curve. Contango (ratio < 1)
is a calm state; backwardation (ratio > 1) is a stressed state. The strategy
trades a long-only TQQQ/BIL book on a hysteresis machine:

| Condition | Target |
|---|---|
| `vr >= 1.05` or `d20 >= +0.10` | 100% BIL |
| `vr <= 0.95` and `d20 <= +0.05` | 100% TQQQ |
| otherwise | hold previous state |

where, for official external closes:

```
vr_t  = VIX_t / VIX3M_t
d20_t = vr_t - vr_{t-20}
```

The 0.95-1.05 level band is the deadband. The 0.05-0.10 change band is the
second deadband: re-entry requires the 20-session change to have cooled to
+0.05, not merely to be below the +0.10 stress trigger. The decision is taken
from the session's official external close, written at the session's 15:59 bar
and filled at the next session's 09:30 open. Bars inside a session carry the
target written at the previous close. Idle capital is BIL.

The centre is a round-number cell (`0.95 / 1.05 / 0.10`, 20 sessions). A coarse
exploration on the same development window preceded the centre; the full 8-cell
box and the 5-day/level-only ablations are reported in section 6 so the reader
can judge the selection.

## 2. Data and execution

- Signal series: Yahoo daily `^VIX` and `^VIX3M` adjusted closes, 2015-01-02
  onward. Both start more than a year before the first development session.
- Execution: local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel, next-session 09:30 open, 2%
  rebalance band, 1 bp headline cost, 5/10 bp sensitivity. The benchmark is
  100% TQQQ on the same panel and cost.
- No 2024+ row is loaded: `vix_features(DEV_END)` truncates both series before
  the ratio is formed. The panel itself ends 2023-12-29.

## 3. Headline development metrics

1-minute panel, next-session open, 2% band. "TQQQ exposure" is the mean TQQQ
weight; the harness "exposure" is 100% because idle capital is BIL.

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | TQQQ exp. | Fills | Turnover | Ending equity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | **48.82%** | **65.45%** | **1.080** | 1.526 | 47.31% | 79.33% | **165** | 1020.1x | $2,390,509 |
| 5 bp | 47.59% | 65.72% | 1.062 | 1.500 | 47.31% | 79.33% | 165 | 974.1x | $2,237,829 |
| 10 bp | 46.07% | 66.07% | 1.040 | 1.469 | 47.32% | 79.33% | 165 | 919.8x | $2,060,619 |
| TQQQ B&H | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.801 | 1.122 | 66.55% | 100% | 1 | 1.0x | $1,175,165 |
| QQQ B&H | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.900 | — | 22.02% | 0% | 1 | 1.0x | $398,628 |
| **TQQQ dev bar** | **36.72%** | **82.29%** | **0.82** | — | — | — | — | — | — |

The strategy clears the bar on all three headline metrics. The 1 bp to 10 bp
cost is 2.75 pp of CAGR. The daily-bar cross-check (same decision clock, one
open/close per session) is 48.41% CAGR / 63.30% DD / 1.061 Sharpe / 165 fills.
The two paths agree within 0.4 pp of CAGR; the 1-minute path has a slightly
deeper intraday drawdown.

## 4. Activity and trade anatomy

| Item | Value |
|---|---:|
| Full-window fills | **165** |
| State changes | **82** (41 entries, 41 exits) |
| TQQQ buys / sells | 42 / 41 |
| Average on-run | 38.0 sessions |
| Median on-run | 28.0 sessions |
| On sessions / fraction | 1,597 / 79.4% |
| State changes by year | 11, 13, 12, 14, 9, 15, 11, 4 (2016-2023) |
| Final state | risk-on |

The strategy is active in every year. The largest number of state changes is
2021 (15), the smallest 2023 (4). The 2022 path is the important one: it went
off on 2022-01-21, re-entered on 2022-02-08, off on 2022-02-10, on 2022-02-15,
off on 2022-03-02, on 2022-03-15, off on 2022-04-26, on 2022-05-20, off on
2022-09-06 and on 2022-11-03. That is a whipsaw through the H1 bear rallies, not
a clean exit.

## 5. Subperiods and yearly returns

| Subperiod | Strategy CAGR | Strategy DD | Strategy Sharpe | TQQQ CAGR | TQQQ DD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 45.91% | 35.69% | 1.240 | 48.60% | 58.0% |
| 2020-2021 | 92.93% | 30.29% | 1.523 | 91.47% | 69.9% |
| 2022-2023 | **14.36%** | **61.58%** | 0.528 | -22.33% | 81.0% |

The strategy roughly matches TQQQ in the two bull subperiods (slightly below in
2016-2019, slightly above in 2020-2021) with much smaller drawdowns, and turns
the 2022-2023 bear from -22.3% CAGR into +14.4% CAGR. But the 2022-2023 path
contains a 61.6% drawdown; the positive subperiod CAGR is driven by 2023, not
by avoiding 2022.

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | QQQ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +26.1% | +18.6% | +9.3% |
| 2017 | +66.6% | +113.0% | +31.5% |
| 2018 | -4.9% | -23.5% | -1.8% |
| 2019 | +109.4% | +130.5% | +38.4% |
| 2020 | +147.9% | +99.8% | +45.9% |
| 2021 | +56.2% | +90.9% | +29.2% |
| 2022 | **-55.9%** | -79.7% | -33.2% |
| 2023 | +202.4% | +204.9% | +55.9% |

The 2022 monthly losses are the honest core of the result: January -35.1%,
April -34.3%, June -27.6%, December -26.5%, August -16.6%. A "crash filter"
that loses 56% in the bear year is not a crash filter. It is a regime overlay
that reduces, but does not remove, bear-market beta.

## 6. 8-cell parameter plateau

The pre-registered 2 x 2 x 2 box around the centre `(0.95, 1.05, 0.10)`:

| `lo` | `hi` | `thr` | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | Clears bar |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|:--:|
| 0.93 | 1.03 | 0.08 | 40.94% | 68.75% | 1.003 | 189 | yes |
| 0.93 | 1.03 | 0.12 | 33.32% | 78.47% | 0.842 | 141 | no |
| 0.93 | 1.07 | 0.08 | 40.94% | 68.75% | 1.003 | 189 | yes |
| 0.93 | 1.07 | 0.12 | 32.33% | 78.47% | 0.824 | 141 | no |
| 0.97 | 1.03 | 0.08 | 51.97% | 57.65% | 1.144 | 205 | yes |
| 0.97 | 1.03 | 0.12 | 42.29% | 73.43% | 0.952 | 149 | yes |
| 0.97 | 1.07 | 0.08 | 51.79% | 57.65% | 1.142 | 205 | yes |
| 0.97 | 1.07 | 0.12 | 42.83% | 73.43% | 0.958 | 145 | yes |
| **centre 0.95/1.05/0.10** | | | **48.82%** | **65.45%** | **1.080** | **165** | **yes** |

Six of eight cells clear the full bar; the two failures are the `thr=0.12`
cells at the lower re-entry level, where the strategy waits too long to
re-enter. The centre is not the box maximum (the 0.97/0.08 cells are higher),
so the result is not a single-cell selection. The `hi` dimension is nearly
inert at 1.03 vs 1.07: the 20-day change trigger, not the inversion level,
does most of the work.

**Ablations.** A 5-day change window gives 26.38% CAGR / 79.36% DD / 0.706
Sharpe / 175 fills: too noisy, fails the bar. Level-only (`vr <= 0.95`) gives
28.62% CAGR / 74.80% DD / 0.775 Sharpe / 341 fills: also fails. The 20-day
change and the hysteresis are both necessary; the signal is not just "long when
VIX is low."

## 7. Placebo / randomized signal dates

Two circular-shift placebos on the daily panel, 500 draws each:

| Placebo | Observed daily CAGR | p-value | 5th pct | Median | 95th pct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shift the VIX/VIX3M series | 48.41% | **0.074** | 8.67% | 25.04% | 51.19% |
| Shift the state path (matched exposure/run lengths) | 48.41% | **0.054** | 9.46% | 25.63% | 48.86% |

The signal-shift p-value is 0.074 and the state-path p-value is 0.054. The
observed CAGR is near the 95th percentile of both placebo distributions. This
is suggestive, not overwhelming: the strategy is long TQQQ 79% of the time, and
a random 79%-long path in this bull market still earns a median 25% CAGR. The
timing adds roughly 23 pp of CAGR over the median random path, but the upper
tail of the placebo distribution is close to the observed result.

## 8. Correlation with the nine existing winners

Daily development returns, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29:

| Winner | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| ratio-froth | 0.567 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.722 |
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.709 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.620 |
| family-session-timing | 0.578 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.556 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.735 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.471 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.653 |

Range **0.471-0.735**, maximum 0.735 (rebalance-flow). This is below the 0.85
overlap threshold. The strategy shares the long-TQQQ beta of the winners, but
its drawdown path is different: it loses less in 2018 and 2022 and more in 2017
and 2021.

## 9. Mechanism check

The economic story is only partly supported:

- **Supported:** the calm-contango state is a good time to hold TQQQ; the
  backwardation/rapid-repricing state is a good time to reduce. The 2018 Q4 and
  2020 Q1 exits both helped.
- **Not supported:** the signal is not a leading crash indicator. In 2022 the
  curve did not invert decisively until the bear was well underway, and the
  re-entry rule repeatedly bought bear-market rallies. The 2022 loss is -55.9%.
- **Not supported:** the edge is not stable across the decade. 2017 (+66.6% vs
  TQQQ +113.0%) and 2021 (+56.2% vs +90.9%) are large opportunity costs.

The term structure is a **regime conditioner**, not a tail hedge. It reduces
the frequency and depth of large losses but does not eliminate them.

## 10. Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|:--:|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 48.82% | yes |
| 1 bp Sharpe > 0.82 | 1.080 | yes |
| 1 bp max DD < 82.29% | 65.45% | yes |
| >= 100 fills or >= 30 state changes | 165 / 82 | yes |
| >= 6 of 8 box cells clear bar | 6 of 8 | yes |
| Placebo p < 0.10 | 0.074 (signal) / 0.054 (state) | yes |
| 2022-2023 CAGR > -25% | +14.36% | yes |
| Max correlation < 0.85 | 0.735 | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 46.07% | yes |

All pre-registered criteria pass. The verdict is nevertheless **qualified**, for
the reasons in section 9: the 2022 drawdown is severe, the placebo is only
marginally significant, and the 2023 result is close to TQQQ buy-and-hold. The
strategy is a legitimate diversifying regime overlay, not a replacement for a
crash filter.

## 11. Holdout recommendation

Send to the one-shot 2024-2026 holdout as a **diversifying regime overlay**,
with the following expectations stated in advance:

- The 2022-type slow bear is the failure mode; a repeat would produce a large
  drawdown even if the strategy beats TQQQ.
- The 2023-type melt-up is the opportunity-cost mode; the strategy should track
  TQQQ closely if the curve stays in contango.
- The result depends on the 20-day change window and the 0.95 re-entry level.
  If the holdout is driven by a different regime, the edge may not persist.

## 12. Reproduction

```
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
$env:BT_THREADS = "4"
python research/new/family-vix-term-structure/strategy.py
```

`strategy.py` exposes `build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` returning the `(n, 3)`
long-only weight matrix and regenerates `result.json` on the development panel.
hypothesis_md:
# VIX term structure — pre-registration

**Family:** `vix-term-structure`  
**Directory:** `research/new/family-vix-term-structure/`  
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29. No 2024-2026 row enters any
feature, result or robustness calculation. External series are truncated at the
development end before the features are computed.  
**Status:** development-only study. The lead runs the one-shot holdout.

## 1. Hypothesis

The implied-volatility curve is a direct price of near-term versus medium-term
uncertainty. When the curve is in **contango** (VIX below VIX3M), near-term
protection is cheap relative to three-month protection: the market is calm and
the marginal buyer of protection is not panicking. When the curve inverts
(VIX above VIX3M), near-term fear is elevated relative to the three-month
outlook: dealers are marking up crash insurance and the equity risk premium is
being repriced. A long TQQQ book should be held in the calm state and moved to
BIL when the curve inverts or when the ratio rises quickly enough to signal a
new stress impulse.

The claim is about the **shape of the index-option surface**, not about price
trend, realised volatility, drawdown, calendar dates, opening-range flow,
machine learning or relative strength. VIX and VIX3M are the only signal inputs.

## 2. Why this is a new family

The primary signal is the VIX/VIX3M ratio. The strategy does not use:

- a 100-250 day moving-average trend gate;
- volatility targeting / vol-of-vol scaling of a price series;
- a drawdown, capitulation or crash event;
- a calendar date window (FOMC, OpEx, turn-of-month, holidays);
- an opening-range, closing-flow or intraday-microstructure signal;
- an ML classifier;
- a QQQ/SPY or TQQQ/QQQ relative-strength gate.

The only price inputs are QQQ/TQQQ/BIL marks for execution. The decision
variable is the implied-vol term structure.

## 3. Exact definitions

For each external close date `t`:

```
vr_t   = VIX_t / VIX3M_t
d20_t  = vr_t - vr_{t-20}
```

`VIX` is the CBOE 30-day implied-volatility index and `VIX3M` the 3-month
index. The external files are Yahoo daily series; for an index the adjusted
close equals the close. Both series start 2015-01-02, so the first 2016
session has more than a full year of warm-up. The feature frame is truncated at
the development end before any feature is calculated. The ratio and its
20-session change are computed on the external calendar and then reindexed to
the QQQ session calendar with a forward fill; no QQQ bar is used to form the
signal.

## 4. State machine and exact rules

A three-condition hysteresis with a deadband:

```
if vr_t >= 1.05  or  d20_t >= +0.10   ->  risk-off  (100% BIL)
elif vr_t <= 0.95  and d20_t <= +0.05 ->  risk-on   (100% TQQQ)
else                                  ->  hold previous state
```

- The **1.05 upper level** is the inversion trigger. The 0.95 lower level is the
  re-entry trigger; the 0.95-1.05 band is the deadband. The state is not
  flipped by a ratio that merely crosses 1.00.
- The **+0.10 20-session change** is the stress-impulse trigger. A ratio that
  rises by 0.10 in a month is a repricing of near-term fear even if the curve
  has not inverted. Re-entry requires the 20-session change to have fallen back
  to +0.05 or less *and* the level to be at or below 0.95, so a bear-market
  rally that only partly normalises the curve does not immediately re-lever.
- An unavailable feature does not trade; the previous state is held.
- The initial state (before the first decision) is risk-on.

The decision is taken from the session's official external close and written
at that session's 15:59 bar; it fills at the next session's 09:30 open. No
intraday information is used. Idle capital is BIL, not cash.

## 5. Pre-registered parameter box

Centre: `lower = 0.95`, `upper = 1.05`, `chg_thr = 0.10`, 20-session change.

The 8-cell plateau is the 2 x 2 x 2 box:

| axis | low | high |
|---|---|---|
| lower level | 0.93 | 0.97 |
| upper level | 1.03 | 1.07 |
| 20-day change trigger | 0.08 | 0.12 |

Every cell must be reported. The centre is a round-number cell inside the box,
not the grid maximum.

## 6. Falsifiers / kill criteria (pre-registered)

The family is rejected if any of the following holds on the development window:

1. **Return:** 1 bp CAGR is below the TQQQ development bar of 36.72%, or the
   Sharpe is below 0.82, or max drawdown is worse than 82.29%.
2. **Activity:** fewer than 100 full fills and fewer than 30 independent state
   changes. A strategy that sits in one state is dead, not defensive.
3. **Plateau:** fewer than 6 of the 8 box cells clear the TQQQ CAGR bar, or the
   centre is the maximum of the box (a knife-edge selection).
4. **Placebo:** circular-shift placebo p-value above 0.10 on CAGR.
5. **Subperiod:** the 2022-2023 CAGR is below -25% while BIL is available; a
   crash filter that still loses a quarter a year in the bear market has not
   isolated the term-structure effect.
6. **Overlap:** correlation above 0.85 with any of the nine existing winners.
7. **Cost:** 10 bp CAGR below the TQQQ 1 bp bar (36.72%), i.e. the edge is
   entirely a zero-cost artefact.

These are stated before the headline run. A negative result is reported as a
negative result.

"""VIX term-structure regime on QQQ, TQQQ and BIL.

Development window only: 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29.

Mechanism
---------
The VIX/VIX3M ratio is the shape of the implied-vol curve.  Contango
(ratio < 1) is a calm regime; backwardation (ratio > 1) is a stressed regime.
The strategy trades a long-only TQQQ/BIL book on a hysteresis machine:

    risk-off  if vr >= 1.05 or  d20 >= +0.10
    risk-on   if vr <= 0.95 and d20 <= +0.05
    hold      otherwise

where vr is VIX/VIX3M and d20 is its 20-session change.  The 0.95-1.05 level
band and the 0.05-0.10 change band are the deadband.  Requiring the 20-day
change to have cooled, not just the level to have fallen, keeps the book out of
bear-market rallies that only partly normalise the curve.

The decision is taken from the session's official external close, written at
that session's 15:59 bar and filled at the next session's 09:30 open.  No
2024+ row is loaded.  Idle capital is BIL, not cash.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "4"
    python research/new/family-vix-term-structure/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402
import external  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")
CQ, CT, CB = 0, 1, 2
BPY_1M = 252 * 390
BPY_1D = 252
BAR = {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229, "sharpe": 0.82}

# Pre-registered centre.
LO = 0.95
HI = 1.05
CHG_T = 0.10
CHG_WIN = 20
BAND = 0.02
SLIPS = (1.0, 5.0, 10.0)

WINNERS = (
    "ratio-froth",
    "vol-scaled-crash-stop",
    "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window",
    "family-session-timing",
    "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow",
    "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# term-structure features
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def vix_features(end: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """VIX/VIX3M ratio and its 20-session change, indexed by external date.

    `end` truncates both series before any feature is computed, so a
    development run never touches a post-development row.
    """
    vix = external.load("^VIX")
    vix3 = external.load("^VIX3M")
    if end is not None:
        vix = vix.loc[:pd.Timestamp(end)]
        vix3 = vix3.loc[:pd.Timestamp(end)]
    vr = (vix / vix3).dropna()
    out = pd.DataFrame(index=vr.index)
    out["vr"] = vr
    out["d20"] = vr.diff(20)
    out["d5"] = vr.diff(5)
    return out


def _machine(vr: pd.Series, d: pd.Series, lower: float = LO, upper: float = HI,
             chg_thr: float = CHG_T, state0: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    """Hysteresis state: 1 = risk-on (TQQQ), 0 = risk-off (BIL)."""
    x = vr.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = d.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    out = np.empty(len(x), dtype=np.int8)
    s = int(state0)
    for i in range(len(x)):
        if np.isfinite(x[i]) and np.isfinite(v[i]):
            if x[i] >= upper or v[i] >= chg_thr:
                s = 0
            elif x[i] <= lower and v[i] <= chg_thr / 2.0:
                s = 1
        out[i] = s
    return out.astype(bool)


def state_series(session_dates: pd.DatetimeIndex, lower: float = LO,
                 upper: float = HI, chg_thr: float = CHG_T,
                 chg_win: int = CHG_WIN, end: str | None = None,
                 feature_override: pd.Series | None = None,
                 return_prior: bool = False):
    """Boolean risk-on state on the QQQ session calendar.

    The feature frame ends at the last session in `session_dates` (or `end`),
    so the run cannot see 2024+ data.  The state for a session is formed from
    that session's official external close and executed at the next open.
    """
    if feature_override is None:
        end = end or str(pd.Timestamp(session_dates[-1]).date())
        feat = vix_features(end)
        vr = feat["vr"]
        d = vr.diff(chg_win)
    else:
        vr = feature_override
        d = vr.diff(chg_win)
    raw = _machine(vr, d, lower, upper, chg_thr)
    s = pd.Series(raw, index=vr.index)
    on = s.reindex(session_dates, method="ffill").to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    prior = s.loc[s.index < session_dates[0]]
    prior_on = bool(prior.iloc[-1]) if len(prior) else True
    if return_prior:
        return on, prior_on
    return on


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, lower: float = LO, upper: float = HI,
                  chg_thr: float = CHG_T, chg_win: int = CHG_WIN,
                  state_override: np.ndarray | None = None,
                  return_state: bool = False):
    """Return the (n, 3) long-only weight matrix (col 1 TQQQ, col 2 BIL).

    A target written at session k's 15:59 bar fills at session k+1's open.
    Bars inside session k carry the target written at session k-1's close.
    """
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3), dtype=float)
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    session_dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates[first])
    if state_override is not None:
        on = np.asarray(state_override, dtype=bool)
        if len(on) != len(first):
            raise ValueError("state_override length does not match sessions")
        prior_on = bool(on[0])
    else:
        on, prior_on = state_series(session_dates, lower, upper, chg_thr,
                                    chg_win, return_prior=True)

    nd = len(first)
    for k in range(nd):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        held = prior_on if k == 0 else bool(on[k - 1])
        w[f:l, CT] = 1.0 if held else 0.0
        w[f:l, CB] = 0.0 if held else 1.0
        w[l, CT] = 1.0 if on[k] else 0.0
        w[l, CB] = 0.0 if on[k] else 1.0

    w[-1] = w[-2]
    if w.min() < -1e-12 or w.sum(axis=1).max() > 1.0 + 1e-9:
        raise AssertionError("invalid weights")
    if return_state:
        return w, on
    return w


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# evaluation helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _pack(s: dict) -> dict:
    keys = ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
            "exposure", "turnover", "fills", "ending_equity", "years")
    return {k: (int(s[k]) if k == "fills" else float(s[k])) for k in keys}


def _session_end_equity(ts, equity):
    dates, _, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    return pd.Series(equity[last], index=pd.to_datetime(dates[last]))


def _subperiod(eq: pd.Series, start, end):
    x = eq.loc[start:end]
    if len(x) < 2:
        return None
    years = (x.index[-1] - x.index[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400)
    rets = x.pct_change().dropna().to_numpy()
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(x.to_numpy())
    return {
        "start": str(x.index[0].date()), "end": str(x.index[-1].date()),
        "cagr": float((x.iloc[-1] / x.iloc[0]) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0),
        "max_drawdown": float(-(x.to_numpy() / peak - 1.0).min()),
        "sharpe": float(np.mean(rets) / np.std(rets) * np.sqrt(BPY_1D))
        if np.std(rets) > 0 else 0.0,
        "total_return": float(x.iloc[-1] / x.iloc[0] - 1.0),
    }


def _trade_stats(ts, on, fill_log):
    entries = int(np.sum((~on[:-1]) & on[1:]))
    exits = int(np.sum(on[:-1] & (~on[1:])))
    runs = []
    cur, ln = bool(on[0]), 1
    for x in on[1:]:
        if bool(x) == cur:
            ln += 1
        else:
            runs.append((cur, ln))
            cur, ln = bool(x), 1
    runs.append((cur, ln))
    on_runs = [ln for flag, ln in runs if flag]
    t_buys = [f for f in fill_log if f["symbol"] == CT and f["side"] == "buy"]
    t_sells = [f for f in fill_log if f["symbol"] == CT and f["side"] == "sell"]
    return {
        "entries_state": entries, "exits_state": exits,
        "state_changes": entries + exits,
        "tqqq_buys": len(t_buys), "tqqq_sells": len(t_sells),
        "avg_on_run_sessions": float(np.mean(on_runs)) if on_runs else 0.0,
        "median_on_run_sessions": float(np.median(on_runs)) if on_runs else 0.0,
        "on_sessions": int(on.sum()), "on_fraction": float(on.mean()),
        "first_tqqq_buy": str(t_buys[0]["ts"]) if t_buys else None,
        "last_tqqq_buy": str(t_buys[-1]["ts"]) if t_buys else None,
        "last_tqqq_sell": str(t_sells[-1]["ts"]) if t_sells else None,
        "final_state": "risk_on" if on[-1] else "risk_off",
    }


def _daily_sim(tsd, od, cd, on):
    tgt = np.column_stack([np.zeros(len(on)), on.astype(float),
                           1.0 - on.astype(float)])
    w = external.daily_targets_to_weights(tsd, tgt)
    r = bt.simulate(tsd, od, cd, w, band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    return bt.stats(r, BPY_1D), w


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main():
    ts, o, c = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min", warmup_days=0)
    w, on = build_weights(ts, o, c, return_state=True)

    runs = {}
    for slip in SLIPS:
        r = bt.simulate(ts, o, c, w, band=BAND, slippage_bps=slip, fill_log=True)
        runs[slip] = (r, bt.stats(r, BPY_1M))

    bench = bt.simulate(ts, o, c, np.tile([0.0, 1.0, 0.0], (len(ts), 1)),
                        band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    b = bt.stats(bench, BPY_1M)
    qbench = bt.simulate(ts, o, c, np.tile([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], (len(ts), 1)),
                         band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    qb = bt.stats(qbench, BPY_1M)

    eq = _session_end_equity(ts, runs[1.0][0]["equity"])
    tqqq_close = _session_end_equity(ts, c[:, CT])
    qqq_close = _session_end_equity(ts, c[:, CQ])

    # Daily cross-check: identical decision clock, one open/close per session.
    tsd, od, cd = bt.panel(SYMBOLS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1D", warmup_days=0)
    wd, ond = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, return_state=True)
    rd = bt.simulate(tsd, od, cd, wd, band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    sd = bt.stats(rd, BPY_1D)
    obs_daily_cagr = sd["cagr"]

    # 8-cell pre-registered plateau (2 x 2 x 2 around the centre).
    cell_cfgs = []
    for lo in (0.93, 0.97):
        for hi in (1.03, 1.07):
            for thr in (0.08, 0.12):
                cell_cfgs.append((lo, hi, thr))
    cell_W = []
    for lo, hi, thr in cell_cfgs:
        cell_W.append(build_weights(ts, o, c, lower=lo, upper=hi, chg_thr=thr))
    cell_res = bt.simulate_many(ts, o, c, cell_W, band=BAND,
                                slippage_bps=1.0, threads=4)
    plateau = {}
    for (lo, hi, thr), rr in zip(cell_cfgs, cell_res):
        s = bt.stats(rr, BPY_1M)
        plateau[f"lo={lo:.2f},hi={hi:.2f},thr={thr:.2f}"] = {
            "cagr": float(s["cagr"]), "max_drawdown": float(s["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s["sharpe"]), "fills": int(s["fills"]),
            "clears_bar": bool(s["cagr"] > BAR["cagr"]
                               and s["max_drawdown"] < BAR["max_drawdown"]
                               and s["sharpe"] > BAR["sharpe"]),
        }

    # Circular-shift placebo on the daily panel.
    dates_d, first_d, _ = bt.day_bounds(tsd)
    session_dates_d = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates_d[first_d])
    feat = vix_features(DEV_END)
    vr = feat["vr"].reindex(session_dates_d, method="ffill")
    base = vr.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(20261127)
    n_shift = 500
    shifts = rng.integers(30, len(base) - 30, n_shift)
    placebo = []
    for sh in shifts:
        shifted = pd.Series(np.roll(base, int(sh)), index=session_dates_d)
        on_p = state_series(session_dates_d, feature_override=shifted)
        s_p, _ = _daily_sim(tsd, od, cd, on_p)
        placebo.append(float(s_p["cagr"]))
    placebo = np.array(placebo)
    p_val = float((1 + np.sum(placebo >= obs_daily_cagr)) / (1 + n_shift))

    # Second placebo: circular shift of the state path itself.  This preserves
    # exposure, run lengths and trade count, so it tests the timing dates rather
    # than the signal distribution.
    state_shifts = rng.integers(30, len(ond) - 30, n_shift)
    placebo_state = []
    for sh in state_shifts:
        s = np.roll(ond, int(sh))
        s_stats, _ = _daily_sim(tsd, od, cd, s)
        placebo_state.append(float(s_stats["cagr"]))
    placebo_state = np.array(placebo_state)
    p_state = float((1 + np.sum(placebo_state >= obs_daily_cagr)) / (1 + n_shift))

    # Correlation with the nine existing winners, on development daily returns.
    strat_ret = eq.pct_change().dropna()
    corrs = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        p = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
        if not p.exists():
            corrs[slug] = None
            continue
        d = json.loads(p.read_text())
        x = pd.Series(d["values"], index=pd.to_datetime(d["dates"]))
        x = x.loc[DEV_START:DEV_END].pct_change().dropna()
        j = strat_ret.index.intersection(x.index)
        corrs[slug] = float(strat_ret.loc[j].corr(x.loc[j]))
    cvals = [v for v in corrs.values() if v is not None]

    subs = {
        "2016_2019": _subperiod(eq, "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
        "2020_2021": _subperiod(eq, "2020-01-01", "2021-12-31"),
        "2022_2023": _subperiod(eq, "2022-01-01", "2023-12-29"),
    }
    yearly = {}
    for y in sorted(set(eq.index.year)):
        s = eq.loc[str(y)]
        t = tqqq_close.loc[str(y)]
        q = qqq_close.loc[str(y)]
        yearly[int(y)] = {
            "strategy": float(s.iloc[-1] / s.iloc[0] - 1.0),
            "tqqq": float(t.iloc[-1] / t.iloc[0] - 1.0),
            "qqq": float(q.iloc[-1] / q.iloc[0] - 1.0),
        }

    out = {
        "strategy": "vix-term-structure-hysteresis",
        "directory": "research/new/family-vix-term-structure",
        "window": {"start": DEV_START, "end": DEV_END, "marks": "1min",
                   "fills": "next session 09:30 open, 2% band", "idle": "BIL"},
        "rules": {
            "vr": "VIX / VIX3M official close",
            "d20": "vr - vr.shift(20)",
            "risk_off": f"vr >= {HI:.2f} or d20 >= +{CHG_T:.2f}",
            "risk_on": f"vr <= {LO:.2f} and d20 <= +{CHG_T / 2:.2f}",
            "deadband": f"level {LO:.2f}-{HI:.2f}; change {CHG_T / 2:.2f}-{CHG_T:.2f}",
            "decision": "official external close; written at 15:59, filled next 09:30 open",
            "no": "price trend, realised-vol target, drawdown event, calendar window, opening range, ML, relative strength",
        },
        "dev": {f"{int(slip)}bp": _pack(runs[slip][1]) for slip in SLIPS},
        "benchmark_tqqq": _pack(b),
        "benchmark_qqq": _pack(qb),
        "exposure_tqqq": float(w[:, CT].mean()),
        "exposure_bil": float(w[:, CB].mean()),
        "trade_stats": _trade_stats(ts, on, runs[1.0][0]["fills_log"]),
        "subperiods": subs,
        "yearly": yearly,
        "plateau": plateau,
        "plateau_clears_bar": int(sum(v["clears_bar"] for v in plateau.values())),
        "placebo": {
            "method": "circular shift of the VIX/VIX3M series, 500 draws, daily panel",
            "observed_daily_cagr": float(obs_daily_cagr),
            "p_value_cagr": p_val,
            "placebo_cagr_p05": float(np.percentile(placebo, 5)),
            "placebo_cagr_p50": float(np.percentile(placebo, 50)),
            "placebo_cagr_p95": float(np.percentile(placebo, 95)),
            "state_shift_p_value_cagr": p_state,
            "state_shift_p05": float(np.percentile(placebo_state, 5)),
            "state_shift_p50": float(np.percentile(placebo_state, 50)),
            "state_shift_p95": float(np.percentile(placebo_state, 95)),
        },
        "correlations": corrs,
        "correlation_min": float(min(cvals)), "correlation_max": float(max(cvals)),
        "daily_crosscheck": {"1bp": _pack(sd)},
        "bar": BAR,
        "kill_criteria": {
            "cagr_above_bar": bool(runs[1.0][1]["cagr"] > BAR["cagr"]),
            "sharpe_above_bar": bool(runs[1.0][1]["sharpe"] > BAR["sharpe"]),
            "dd_below_bar": bool(runs[1.0][1]["max_drawdown"] < BAR["max_drawdown"]),
            "activity_floor": bool(runs[1.0][1]["fills"] >= 100
                                   or _trade_stats(ts, on, runs[1.0][0]["fills_log"])["state_changes"] >= 30),
            "plateau_at_least_6": bool(sum(v["clears_bar"] for v in plateau.values()) >= 6),
            "placebo_p_below_010": bool(p_val < 0.10),
            "subperiod_2022_2023_above_minus_25": bool(subs["2022_2023"]["cagr"] > -0.25),
            "max_corr_below_085": bool(max(cvals) < 0.85),
            "cost_10bp_above_bar": bool(runs[10.0][1]["cagr"] > BAR["cagr"]),
        },
    }
    out["kill_criteria"]["all_pass"] = all(out["kill_criteria"].values())
    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + "\n")

    print(json.dumps({
        "dev": out["dev"], "benchmark_tqqq": out["benchmark_tqqq"],
        "exposure_tqqq": out["exposure_tqqq"],
        "trade_stats": out["trade_stats"], "subperiods": out["subperiods"],
        "yearly": out["yearly"], "plateau": out["plateau"],
        "placebo": out["placebo"], "correlations": out["correlations"],
        "daily_crosscheck": out["daily_crosscheck"],
        "kill_criteria": out["kill_criteria"],
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
